integrity: The finite closure graph through length fifteen is exhaustive because each directive step strictly increases length. Minimum attractor sizes are recomputed by two occurrence-based finite engines, and the complete first equality layer is replayed from the closure definitions.
scientific_limitations: The result classifies only the first length at which a binary generalized pseudostandard prefix needs four string-attractor positions. It does not give a universal attractor bound, classify later prefixes, or enumerate all directive descriptions of each word.
title: Length \(15\) is the first four-attractor generalized pseudostandard layer
